title: Testing & security
subtitle: Test behavior and protect API access.
description: Write unit tests for business rules and integration tests with Testcontainers. Configure JWT resource-server security and test invalid input, insufficient permissions, and missing resources.

lessons.title: Unit tests for business rules
lessons.summary: Test services and domain objects with fakes without loading Spring. Keep results repeatable.
objectives: Inject time so date-based tests are deterministic.
keyPoints: Test observable behavior rather than every internal call.
Use fakes and stubs at dependency boundaries.
practice: Test discount behavior and negative order totals without Spring.
The tests run quickly and report the same result on every date.

exercises.prompt: Complete a test asserting that an Order with a negative total throws IllegalArgumentException.
checks: Create new Order(...) inside the lambda
exercises.explanation: assertThrows fails when the expected exception is not raised and also lets you inspect the returned exception.
Arrange the objects, perform one action, then assert an observable result.

exercises.prompt: A service uses LocalDate.now() for a promotion. How should its test control the date?
options: Inject Clock and use Clock.fixed in the test.
Only run the test on the promotion date.
exercises.explanation: Time is a dependency. Passing a fixed Clock avoids tests that change with the calendar.

lessons.title: Integration tests with a database
lessons.summary: Testcontainers runs real PostgreSQL during tests so mappings, SQL, migrations, and constraints are tested together.
objectives: Explain differences between H2 and PostgreSQL.
keyPoints: Static Container fields can share a database across a test class.
ServiceConnection supplies connection settings from the container.
Use the production database technology for dialect-specific behavior.
practice: Run a repository integration test against a PostgreSQL container.
Flyway runs and the test exercises real PostgreSQL constraints and queries.

exercises.prompt: Complete the PostgreSQL container declaration so Spring Boot configures the test datasource automatically.
exercises.explanation: ServiceConnection obtains datasource settings from the container. Replace.NONE keeps a JPA slice from substituting an embedded database.

exercises.prompt: Why use PostgreSQL through Testcontainers when production uses PostgreSQL rather than relying only on H2?
options: SQL dialects, types, and constraints differ, so an H2 test can pass while production fails.
Containers are always faster than H2.
Spring Boot does not support H2.
exercises.explanation: PostgreSQL-specific features and migration syntax need to be exercised on PostgreSQL.

lessons.title: Authentication, authorization & JWT
lessons.summary: The API validates tokens from an authorization server and checks whether their scopes permit each operation.
objectives: Verify signatures rather than only decoding payloads.
keyPoints: 401 indicates missing or invalid authentication; 403 indicates insufficient permission.
Spring maps scopes to authorities with a SCOPE_ prefix.
Base64 decoding does not prove who issued a token.
practice: Require orders:write for POST /orders and verify tokens against your issuer.
Missing tokens return 401, insufficient scopes return 403, and allowed requests reach the controller.

exercises.prompt: A valid token with orders:read calls POST /orders, which requires orders:write. Which status is appropriate?
exercises.explanation: The caller is authenticated but lacks permission for this operation, so the response is 403.

exercises.prompt: Configure SecurityFilterChain: POST /orders needs SCOPE_orders:write, all other requests require authentication, and JWT resource-server support is enabled.
exercises.explanation: Rules are evaluated in order. Put specific rules before anyRequest and configure the expected issuer.

exercises.prompt: A filter decodes a JWT payload and trusts its sub claim without verifying the signature. What is wrong?
options: Anyone can forge a payload and claim any user identity.
exercises.explanation: Encoding is not verification. Use the resource server to verify the signature and expected token claims.

lessons.title: Tests for failure scenarios
lessons.summary: Check 400, 401, 403, and 404 responses so refactoring does not silently change validation or access rules.
objectives: Write a MockMvc test for a missing token.
Test error responses as part of the API contract.
Evaluate test scenarios beyond coverage percentages.
keyPoints: WebMvcTest loads a web slice and lets the service be mocked.
Test each meaningful status and security condition.
High line coverage does not prove error handling works.
practice: Add HTTP tests for invalid input, missing credentials, insufficient scope, and a missing order.
CI fails if the relevant status or access behavior changes unexpectedly.

exercises.prompt: Complete a MockMvc test asserting that GET /orders/1 without a token returns 401.
exercises.explanation: Add authenticated variants with appropriate scopes to test success and forbidden responses separately.

exercises.prompt: Coverage is 95%, but no tests assert 400, 401, 403, or 404. What is the risk?
options: Security or error-mapping changes can pass without being detected.
exercises.explanation: Coverage records executed lines. Explicit assertions for failure scenarios check the contract clients actually depend on.
